input_references.role: Timestamped, road-aligned GPS observations for each taxi trajectory

metadata.goal: Analyze recurrent operating routes in the provided Porto taxi trajectories and summarize their spatial, temporal, and passenger-request characteristics.
metadata.category: Recurrent route structure and passenger-request behavior
metadata.dataset_description: A constructed Porto Taxi case spanning two working weeks. It contains 140 road-aligned passenger trajectories: 105 distributed across recurrent corridors and 35 spatially diverse background trips. The trip table and GPS points support identifying route structure, orientation, occurrence time, and request-source composition.

insight_list.insight: Five recurrent trajectory patterns can be identified in the provided taxi traces, each representing a repeatedly observed movement corridor in Porto.

plot.title: Five Recurrent Taxi Movement Corridors
plot.description: Road-aligned trajectories reveal five repeatedly occupied movement corridors against a diverse non-recurrent background.

insight_list.question: What recurrent movement corridors can be identified from the spatial shapes of the provided taxi trajectories, and which trips do not belong to these recurring patterns?
insight_list.code: # Cluster trajectories from trajectory_points.csv by spatial similarity, then map the resulting clusters.

insight_list.insight: Four of the five recurrent trajectory patterns are predominantly north–south oriented, whereas the remaining pattern is predominantly east–west oriented.

plot.title: Orientation of Recurrent Taxi Patterns
plot.description: Endpoint-displacement components distinguish north–south from east–west recurrent corridors.

insight_list.question: How does the dominant orientation of each recurrent trajectory pattern compare across the identified corridors?

insight_list.insight: The recurrent patterns have distinct temporal preferences: Patterns 1–3 occur predominantly on weekday mornings, while Patterns 4–5 are concentrated on weekday evenings.

plot.title: Weekday Temporal Preferences of Recurrent Patterns
plot.description: The heatmap compares when the inferred route patterns occur on weekdays.

insight_list.question: When during weekdays does each recurrent trajectory pattern occur, and do the patterns separate into morning and evening groups?

insight_list.insight: All five recurrent patterns have similar passenger-request compositions: approximately 80% of trips originate from street hails and 20% from phone-dispatched calls.

plot.title: Passenger Request Types Across Recurrent Patterns
plot.description: Each inferred corridor is compared by street-hail and phone-dispatched request shares.

insight_list.question: Do passenger request types differ across the recurrent movement patterns, or are their call-type compositions similar?

insights: Five recurrent trajectory patterns can be identified in the provided taxi traces, each representing a repeatedly observed movement corridor in Porto.
Four of the five recurrent trajectory patterns are predominantly north–south oriented, whereas the remaining pattern is predominantly east–west oriented.
The recurrent patterns have distinct temporal preferences: Patterns 1–3 occur predominantly on weekday mornings, while Patterns 4–5 are concentrated on weekday evenings.
All five recurrent patterns have similar passenger-request compositions: approximately 80% of trips originate from street hails and 20% from phone-dispatched calls.
summary: The trajectories organize into five recurring operating corridors. Four are predominantly north–south, while the east–west crosstown corridor is the remaining pattern. Patterns 1–3 are concentrated in weekday mornings, whereas Patterns 4–5 occur in weekday evenings. Across the corridors, passenger-request composition remains street-hail dominant and similar.
